column3: Nearly repeats the focus's sequence: seeing what was promised reveals whose supporters and number are weaker.
A hostile crowd calls Shuayb weak in a historical dispute, without the focus's eschatological reversal.
Satan's deceptive promises illuminate the contrast with the true promise whose reality the misguided will see.
Its unrelated command to extend a rope shares wording but does not develop reprieve, punishment, or the Hour.
Immediately precedes the focus: unbelievers boast of the better station and gathering that the focus overturns.
Affirms that God's promise through His messengers is not broken, supporting certainty of the promised final outcome.
Those led astray see the punishment, conceal remorse, and receive recompense, directly anticipating the focus's exposure.
The command for Moses to travel by night does not clarify misguidance, reprieve, or the promised final event.
Shows misguiding others ultimately harms the misleaders themselves, a related consequence of misguidance.
Uses the same announcement that people will know who is in clear misguidance, directly paralleling the focus's final disclosure.
Immediately before the focus, it recalls communities with superior possessions and appearance who were destroyed.
Extended wealth offers a limited worldly parallel to the focus's extended reprieve in misguidance.
Directly joins delayed punishment, seeing what was promised, and the eventual destruction of the defiantly wicked.
An army's drowning supplies a historical image of organized forces proving powerless before divine judgment.
The extended pillars of Hell punishment share only the idea of extension, not the focus's argument.
Explicitly calls condemned people worse in position and more astray, closely echoing the focus's reversal of status.
The immediate continuation contrasts God's increase of the guided with the better reward and return of lasting good deeds.
The account of mighty armies gives only a broad context for the focus's claim about weaker forces.
Same-surah continuation: a denier is granted an extension of punishment, sharpening the focus's extended reprieve.
The numbered guardians of the Fire relate to the focus's reference to forces, within a punishment setting.
God sends unseen forces and punishes unbelievers, a related contrast to reliance on merely apparent troops.
The misguided see the punishment and seek a way back, directly matching the focus's moment of realization.
Inevitable death and return to the Knower culminate in disclosure of deeds, a broad final-account counterpart.
Identifies idols as a source of widespread misguidance, clarifying the state named in the focus.
The prayer explicitly asks to be shown what the deniers are promised, closely matching the focus's seeing motif.
The Friday-prayer instruction has no material relation to the focus's eschatological warning.
Declares both seeker and sought weak, supporting the focus's exposure of supposedly supporting powers as weak.
Directly explains the Hour's certain but divinely timed arrival, one of the two promised outcomes in the focus.
God alone knows His forces and appoints the Fire's guardians, contextualizing the focus's comparison of forces.
Joseph's brothers call their father misguided while claiming group strength, a limited ironic parallel to false judgment.
Sets guidance against those upon whom misguidance became due and directs attention to the deniers' outcome.
People emerge so their deeds may be shown to them, a general counterpart to seeing the consequences promised.
Records the deniers' dismissal of what they are promised, directly contrasting their later unavoidable realization.
Those driven to Hell are explicitly worse in place and more astray in way, closely matching both focus verdicts.
Seeing trade and amusement concerns abandoning the sermon, not the promised punishment or Hour.
God's hosts in heaven and earth provide a theological contrast to the allegedly strong human forces in the focus.
Joseph's statement that his brothers are worse in position supplies a moral, non-eschatological status reversal.
The defeat of the Elephant army is a distant historical example of troops failing before divine action.
Names those disputing the Hour as far astray while believers know it is true, directly supporting the focus's contrast.
Describes choosing misguidance over guidance and punishment over forgiveness, directly linking misguidance to the Fire.
Failure to carry the Torah and God's not guiding wrongdoers only broadly relate to being left in misguidance.
The gathered forces of Iblis offer a related image of organized false support, though without the focus's final verdict.
Wrongdoers see the punishment, hide regret, and are judged with justice, closely paralleling the focus's event.
Challenges the unbelievers' supposed army that could aid them against the Most Merciful, directly echoing weak forces.
Those in the Fire call for doubled punishment for those who led them there, extending the focus's punishment theme.
Commands leaving deniers to play until they meet their promised day, directly paralleling the focus's delayed reprieve.
God extends the hypocrites in their transgression as they wander blindly, closely matching extension in misguidance.
Commands leaving deniers in diversion until they meet their promised day, directly parallel to the focus's sequence.
God's hosts belong to Him, providing a broader contrast to the focus's inadequate human troops.
Idris being raised to a high place does not clarify the focus's threat or reversal of worldly standing.
God's own forces are victorious, supplying a direct theological contrast to the focus's weak opposing forces.
Sets the human response as grateful or ungrateful after guidance, a limited counterpart to the focus's two outcomes.
Warns that part of a messenger's promised threat may reach the deniers and links excess to lack of guidance.
Explicitly joins the Fire with the Hour and a severer punishment, directly developing both promised outcomes.
Declares God's promise true despite most people not knowing, directly grounding the focus's promised event.
The Hour arrives suddenly, exposing deniers' loss and regret, directly supporting the focus's eventual realization.
Forbids thinking God will fail His promise and names His retribution, directly confirming the focus's warning.
A sudden sea crisis produces recognition of helplessness, only distantly echoing eventual realization of divine power.
Identifies Hell as that which the deniers were promised, directly naming the focus's threatened punishment.
Describes purchasing misguidance and seeking others' misguidance, directly clarifying the focus's condition.
Moses calls Satan an openly misleading enemy in a historical incident, only broadly related to misguidance.
The command of the Hour is as swift as a glance and God is fully capable, directly supporting its certainty.
Extended shade in Paradise does not develop the focus's extension in misguidance or its threatened outcome.
Denial of the Hour amid presumed privilege is answered by disclosure of deeds and severe punishment, closely parallel.
Noah's appeal to God's true promise concerns the scope of familial rescue, not the focus's threatened promise.
Explicitly portrays people as buying misguidance for guidance and failing to profit, directly clarifying the focus's state.
A denier rejects the resurrection promise despite being told God's promise is true, directly anticipating the focus's outcome.
The instruction to worship God and honor parents is unrelated to the focus's eschatological warning.
Ishmael's truthfulness to a promise is only a lexical and ethical contrast to God's certain promised judgment.
Envy's evil does not clarify misguidance, the Hour, or apparent forces.
Those following desire without knowledge are misled and have no helpers, directly related to the focus's weak support.
Mary's withdrawal to an eastern place does not develop the focus's themes.
Deniers challenge the timing of the promise, directly contrasting with the focus's assurance that it will be seen.
Contrasts the guided with those for whom misguidance became due while they think themselves guided.
The Lord knows who has strayed and who is guided, directly supporting the focus's final determination of condition.
The darkness when it settles has no material relation to the focus.
Contrasts one person's guidance with another's misguidance and culminates in the shared return and disclosure of deeds.
Leaves people to God's decision whether to punish or accept repentance, paralleling the focus's either-or judgment frame.
God's intended reversal for the oppressed gives a historical counterpart to the focus's overturning of apparent power.
The Most Merciful's unseen promise is certain to come, supporting the focus's promise under the same divine name.
Calls worship of false gods clear misguidance, directly clarifying the focus's central condition.
Pharaoh and his troops are seized and drowned, a direct historical example of forces proving powerless.
The parable of a burned garden and weak heirs does not clarify the focus's warning.
Seeking refuge from a satanic provocation does not materially develop the focus's final misguidance and punishment.
Identifies a promised outcome for the Day of Account, supporting the focus's certainty of a final appointment.
The instruction for gentle speech while awaiting mercy is unrelated to the focus.
Its reference to prior misguidance occurs in pilgrimage instructions and adds little to the focus.
Seeking refuge from satanic prompting does not clarify the focus's final warning.
The people of Hell admit rejecting a warner and calling the messengers greatly astray, a related reversal of judgment.
Sets the fearlessness of the God-conscious against the warning-bearing mission to humanity, a broad counterpart to misguidance.
The account of parental care, maturity, and gratitude does not illuminate the focus.
Those whom God lets stray have no protecting helpers or escape route, directly reinforcing the focus's weak support.
Distorting words and disobedience lead to curse, but this does not directly develop the focus's promised outcome.
States that the Lord knows best who strayed and who are guided, directly paralleling the focus's decisive disclosure.
God's hearing and knowledge alone do not materially clarify the focus.
After truth arrives, guidance and misguidance return upon each person, directly framing the focus's condition and consequence.
Jacob's grief over Joseph does not relate to the focus's warning.
Those who set up rivals to mislead are told to enjoy briefly before their destination in the Fire, closely parallel.
Abraham's prayer for his family near the Sacred House does not clarify the focus.
Pharaoh's elevation rests on dividing and weakening people, offering a historical contrast to the focus's reversal of power.
The denier's claim that he will receive wealth and children continues the same-surah exposure of worldly status as false security.
Challenges the basis of the denier's confidence in an unseen future, immediately qualifying his worldly claim.
God inherits the wealth and claim in question while the denier comes alone, directly reversing confidence in possessions and supporters.
Those who take gods for honor illustrate the false sources of status and backing exposed by the focus.
The alleged gods will reject their worshippers and become adversaries, directly overturning their hoped-for support.
God sends devils to incite the disbelievers, providing a same-surah mechanism for their deepening misguidance.
Commands patience and says God is only counting their days, closely paralleling the focus's measured extension.
The gathering of the God-conscious before the Most Merciful supplies the positive counterpart to the focus's misguided people.
Criminals are driven to Hell in thirst, directly developing the punishment anticipated in the focus.
A brief worldly enjoyment is followed by compulsion to the Fire, directly paralleling reprieve before punishment.
God's granting of time to disbelievers is not good for them but increases sin before humiliating punishment.
Warns against being deceived by the unbelievers' movement and success in the land, supporting the focus's reversal of apparent standing.
Calls worldly enjoyment small and identifies Hell as the unbelievers' final lodging, completing the contrast with present display.
After worldly openings make people rejoice, God seizes them suddenly and leaves them despairing, a direct reprieve-and-reversal pattern.
The warning to jinn and humans about their meeting with God supplies the final-account frame for the focus's threat.
God gradually draws deniers on from where they do not know, closely matching extension within misguidance.
God grants the deniers respite while His plan remains firm, directly supporting the focus's delayed judgment.
No soul can hasten or postpone its appointed term, clarifying the fixed timing of the promised punishment or Hour.
Challenges deniers about punishment arriving by night or day, directly extending the warning of what they will see.
Worldly enjoyment is brief before return to God and severe punishment for disbelief, matching the focus's temporary reprieve.
If punishment is delayed to a numbered community, deniers mock its postponement until the threatened event surrounds them.
Promises that the deniers will know whom degrading punishment reaches and who receives lasting punishment.
God gives disbelievers respite and then seizes them, a concise historical formulation of delayed retribution.
God delays wrongdoers only until the Day when eyes stare, directly denying that the postponed threat has failed.
God delays people for their wrongdoing to an appointed term, providing the broader rule behind the focus's extension.
God may defer punishment because of mercy, but the wrongdoers have a fixed appointment from which they cannot escape.
Destroyed towns had a fixed appointment for their ruin, providing a historical parallel to divinely timed judgment.
Commands mutual waiting and says they will know who follows the sound path and who is guided, closely echoing final disclosure.
People demand the punishment hastened, while God promises to show His signs, directly framing the delayed threat.
The Hour will come suddenly and confound the deniers, directly developing the focus's promised Hour.
God does not fail His promise even though people ask for punishment to be hastened; a divine day has its own measure.
God gives many wrongdoing towns respite before seizing them, a direct pattern of delayed retribution.
Challenges the assumption that extended wealth and sons mean God is hastening good for the deniers.
Rejects the deniers' reading of extended wealth and children as favor, directly clarifying the focus's extension.
Those who deny the Hour are met with the prepared Blaze, directly linking disbelief in the Hour to punishment.
Warns that part of the punishment the deniers seek to hasten may already be near them.
Deniers ask for punishment to be hastened, though Hell will encompass them, directly extending the focus's threat.
On the Day of Decision, faith will not benefit those who disbelieved and they will not be reprieved.
The promised Day has an appointment that cannot be delayed or advanced, directly clarifying its fixed timing.
God postpones humankind to an appointed term rather than immediately seizing them for wrongdoing.
Deniers challenge the timing of the promise, directly contrasting with the focus's assurance of its realization.
A single blast seizes the disputing deniers, supplying the sudden arrival that follows their challenge.
Promises that the deniers will know who receives humiliating and lasting punishment, closely echoing the focus's final knowledge.
The disbelievers are driven in groups to Hell, directly portraying the punishment promised in the focus.
Affirms that the Hour is certainly coming despite most people's disbelief.
Knowledge of the Hour belongs to God, reinforcing the certainty and divine control of the event.
The Book and balance are sent down in truth, and the Hour may be near, directly reinforcing the looming promised event.
The deniers await only the Hour's sudden arrival while they are unaware.
Deniers call the true promise and the Hour uncertain, directly articulating the disbelief answered by the focus.
The evil consequences of their deeds become apparent to the deniers and the mocked punishment encompasses them.
The deniers await only the sudden Hour, whose signs have already come.
The trumpet comes with the promised reality, directly naming the transition from warning to fulfilled event.
The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split, directly reinforcing the imminence of the focus's promised Hour.
The Hour is the deniers' appointment and is more terrible and bitter, directly intensifying the focus's threat.
When the promised punishment is seen near, the faces of disbelievers are distressed and they are told this is what they sought.
God will gradually draw on those who deny the discourse from where they do not know, closely matching extension in misguidance.
God grants the deniers respite while His plan remains firm, directly parallel to the focus's measured delay.
The deniers see the promised Day as distant, directly contrasting with the divine certainty of its approach.
God sees the promised Day as near, completing the contrast with the deniers' false assessment.
People emerge from graves in haste on the Day they were promised, directly depicting its fulfillment.
Humbled eyes and covered humiliation mark the Day they were promised, directly extending the focus's final exposure.
The Prophet does not know whether what is promised is near or whether God sets a longer term, directly matching deferred fulfillment.
Certainty finally comes to the deniers of judgment, directly naming the end of their denial.
The Day of Decision has a fixed appointment, directly supporting the focus's specified future outcome.
Deniers of the Day of Recompense supply the moral class whose eventual judgment the focus announces.
Mockers call believers astray when they see them, a reversal motif relevant to the focus's final exposure of who is astray.
Certain knowledge will replace denial, preparing for the sight of the Fire.
The Fire will certainly be seen, directly matching the focus's seeing of promised punishment.
The Fire will be seen with the eye of certainty, directly intensifying the focus's realization motif.
